title: Tenant Switch
rule: the navigation is the multi-tenant switcher he builds
description: The portfolio is one light app shell with a workspace switcher. Each employer or client is a workspace with its own projects, role and accent; switching it changes the data and the tint, and the controls stay where they are.
signature: Public Sans with JetBrains Mono for counts and years, one neutral light palette. A top-bar switcher (click, arrow key or Cmd+K) lists the five workspaces from projects.ts with their periods and counts, and its search also finds projects in every workspace. Switching re-tints the shell through one registered --ts-accent (260 ms), replaces the rows with a short staggered fade (220 ms, ease-out, 18 ms steps, at most 8), fades the proof card and rolls the count; focus returns to the switcher, and a keyboard switch only fades for 120 ms. The page filter searches only the current workspace and offers the other workspaces that match, as a tenant-scoped app does. Rows carry an outcome; the proof panel shows real Vianova care and Design System v2 screens (invented data), public screenshots for public products, Problem, Result and Role. Phone: the selected row opens in place and the tapped row holds its position. The state is in the URL (?w=, ?p=).
holdback: Lowest: original, 5/10. The idea (the navigation is the tenant switcher he builds) is new for a portfolio, but the surface is a well-made SaaS admin page: top bar, table, side panel. A visitor who does not open the switcher sees a good product list, not a new form. Hooks is 6: the memorable moment (the whole shell re-tints and the role changes when the workspace changes) needs one click, and the first screen does not show it.
